a mechanism hypothesis that could invalidate part of the projects zero-clear conclusion is now under test. RL training carries shoot_pulse_period 48 in its frozen configs, but a grep of tools/rl/v410_student_eval.py finds the strings shoot and pulse ZERO times: the evaluator only builds (cand, bomb=0) and sends candidate actions. If the evaluator never releases SHOOT then stage_clear is mechanically unreachable at deployment time, and therefore some part of the accumulated 0/120 DAgger plus 0/40 six-arm RL clear counts would be a measurement artefact rather than a capability statement. A bounded diagnostic is dispatched: read the evaluator and the engine control protocol to determine who owns the SHOOT bit and whether any release path exists, then replay the known-clearing recorded trajectory THROUGH the evaluator action channel and check whether it clears, checking the three numbers against 2631430 versus 141379 score and 13195 versus 13272 frames. If replaying through the evaluator cannot clear while adding a pulse can, the mechanism hypothesis holds; the task is then to specify the minimal fix and the list of existing numbers that would need re-testing, WITHOUT changing any implementation and WITHOUT re-running any capability evaluation.

the mechanism hypothesis is CONFIRMED by replaying one and the same recorded trajectory through two action channels. With the shoot pulse the trajectory clears: stage_clear true, score 2631430, frames 13195, stop_reason stage_clear, 0 deaths. Through the EVALUATOR action channel the same trajectory does NOT clear: stage_clear false, score 163945, frames 15564, stop_reason game_over, 3 deaths. The evaluator log shows the stall signature explicitly, score frozen at 141379 from 8000 frames through 12000 frames, and reports shoot_rising_edges 1 versus many under the pulse. So stage_clear is mechanically unreachable through the evaluator action pipeline: the engine needs a SHOOT rising edge to leave the pre-clear state and the evaluator never produces one. Consequence: every zero-clear figure produced through that evaluator cannot be used as evidence about capability, because the graded event could not occur by construction. That covers the 0 of 120 DAgger count (3 rounds x 2 rulers x 20) and the 0 of 240 RL count (6 arms x 2 rulers x 20). G420-4 as graded is therefore INVALID rather than failed_valid: the measuring instrument cannot emit the event it grades. What is untouched: every frame-based number, because frames are observed directly and do not depend on the clear bit, so the six-arm ordering, the DAgger three-round ordering, the R0 prior, the budget saturation and the R4 verdict on PPO coefficients all stand as written. What is undone is the stronger claim that capability exploration was exhausted, because the target event was never actually measured.

the user asked why the model never learned to collect P items and pointed at two mechanics: collecting P, and moving to the upper half to auto-collect everything on screen, plus the defensive consequence that low power means weak shots, so small enemies survive longer, more bullets, and earlier death. The question is answerable from the code and the answer is that the reward has NO power term at all. The complete r3 reward is stage_clear_bonus 1.0, death_penalty 0.25, bomb_penalty 0.1, progress_total 0.5 with progress_score_full 2631430, survive_per_decision 1.2e-05, first_life_per_decision 3.7890269778720825e-05 and first_life_cap 0.25. A grep for power, item, drop or collect across rl.py finds only unrelated hits, including the GAE code that uses the word power for gamma-lambda powers. Meanwhile the ENGINE ALREADY EXPOSES power as a state field: touhou_rl/v400/gym/protocol.py line 336 declares power: float right next to lives: int and bombs: float, so a power term is directly available to the reward exactly as lives and bombs are. Two further facts compound it: the observation play tensor is 4x112x96 against a 640x480 game, so a roughly 16 pixel item sprite lands on about 2.8 by 2.7 pixels and is barely visible, and the reward only pays for survival in TIME, via survive_per_decision and first_life_per_decision, never for having power. So the policy receives no gradient whatsoever toward collecting P, and the user identified a defect of exactly the same class as the first-death blindness that was already found and repaired earlier in this session: the reward cannot see a quantity the ruler cares about. Plausibly this also explains a large part of the measured survival shortfall, since every RL arm dies at 1600 to 1900 frames while a clear needs 13195, and a permanently weak shot would leave enemies alive long enough to saturate the screen.

r4 is dispatched on the user observation that the model never learns to collect P items. The finding that motivates it is already recorded: the r3 reward has no power term at all, while the engine already exposes power as a float next to lives and bombs at protocol.py line 336, so adding the term needs no new data. r4 keeps all seven r3 coefficients byte-identical and adds exactly one term, power_gain, which pays only for positive deltas in power and never penalises a decrease, with w_power bounded fail-closed by w_power times power_max times T_max staying at or below 0.25 times progress_total so it cannot override the task objective. The design deliberately splits the question in two. Half of it is behavioural: does the arm actually collect more power per episode than r3, measured either from r3 payload or from an r3 control arm run in the same block. The other half, which is the one that could invalidate the whole idea, is OBSERVABILITY: a probe over at least fifty real samples must show whether power can be read out of the hud 1x56x160 tensor and the play 4x112x96 tensor, reported as R-squared and MAE, because if power is not legible in the observation then adding a reward term cannot teach anything. At 640x480 downsampled to 112x96 an item sprite of about sixteen pixels lands on roughly 2.8 by 2.7 pixels, so this is a live risk rather than a formality. Four branches are pre-registered, including branch two which would say power does rise but survival does not improve, meaning power is NOT the bottleneck for the 9281-frame shortfall. Measured from pilot-r4-a.json: power_gain 9e-08 and power_max 128.0, so the maximum power reward any single episode can earn is 9e-08 times 128 = 1.152e-05. Against the other reward terms that is negligible by four orders of magnitude: death_penalty 0.25 is 21701 times larger, survive_total_at_horizon 0.119322 is 10358 times larger, progress_total 0.5 is 43403 times larger, first_life_cap 0.25 is 21701 times larger and stage_clear 1.0 is 86806 times larger.
